# Assimp — vendored

    upstream  https://github.com/assimp/assimp
    tag       v5.4.3
    licence   BSD-3-Clause — see LICENSE, which ships in the app bundle
    built     static, arm64 + x86_64, macOS 13 deployment target

## Why at all

FBX. Nothing on macOS reads it, and the format's own SDK is Autodesk's, which
is commercial and carries redistribution terms. Assimp is BSD-3 and reads FBX
in both its binary and ASCII spellings, so it is the only way to open one of
these files in a shipped, source-available app.

## Why only FBX

Configured with `ASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_IMPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF` and
`ASSIMP_BUILD_FBX_IMPORTER=ON`, so the build enables exactly one format:

    Enabled importer formats: FBX

Everything else Assimp can read — OBJ, PLY, STL, COLLADA, glTF — is already
read by SceneKit or by GLTFKit2, and a second reader for a format that already
opens is a second set of quirks to explain when the two disagree. All exporters
are off: this is a viewer.

The result is 6.0 MB for both architectures. With every importer on it is
several times that, for formats nothing would route here.

## How it is built

    cmake -B build -G Ninja \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_IMPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_BUILD_FBX_IMPORTER=ON \
      -DASSIMP_BUILD_ALL_EXPORTERS_BY_DEFAULT=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_BUILD_ASSIMP_TOOLS=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_INSTALL=OFF \
      -DASSIMP_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=OFF \
      -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="arm64;x86_64" \
      -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=13.0 \
      -DCMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5
    cmake --build build --target assimp

The archive and the headers are checked in rather than the source, for the
reason `SwiftTerm/VENDOR.md` gives: the app is one `swiftc` invocation and has
no CMake in it, so a build must not need one. `config.h` and `revision.h` are
generated by that configure step and are copied in beside the shipped headers.

`module.modulemap` is ours — Assimp does not ship one — and exposes the C API
only. Assimp is C++ inside; everything it offers across this boundary is C.

Linked with `-lz`: assimp's FBX reader inflates compressed geometry through
zlib, which macOS already has.

## What was changed from upstream

Nothing in the sources. Only which importers the build enables.
